name: Harms Study Group registries (adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and other pediatric spinal deformity)
what: the Harms Study Group's prospective multicentre registries of pediatric spinal deformity, run with the Setting Scoliosis Straight Foundation: the adolescent idiopathic scoliosis registry, which the group calls the largest AIS database, with cerebral palsy, Scheuermann's kyphosis and Marfan syndrome registries beside it and a quality improvement registry; about twenty years of surgical cases from 37 member surgeons; whether the standing radiographs themselves are shared, or only the measurements taken from them, is not stated on the site and is what the request asks
level_truth: to confirm: standing coronal and lateral films of operated scoliosis patients, before and after surgery, with the instrumented levels known from the operative record, if the images are shared
licence: not recorded; the Database User Program page lists a research tool at USD 5,000 a year (database user access and hosting) and custom research database building at USD 50,000 to 150,000; the terms of a data release are not on the site
how_to_get: The owner's reply to Ali Uneri (Johns Hopkins) accepted his offer of an introduction, and on 2026-10-23 he introduced the owner to Michelle Marks, Executive/Research Director of Setting Scoliosis Straight (mmarks@ssshsg.org, 619-810-1430, San Diego); the group's other addresses are info@ssshsg.org and, on the Database User Program page's button, mpetcharaporn@ssshsg.org.

letters/hsg_ais_registry.md went to her on 2026-10-23 as the owner's reply in the introduction thread: whether the de-identified radiographs can be shared with a research user, through the Database User Program or otherwise, under what agreement and at what cost; the agreement and any fee are the owner's hand.
A yes brings a data use agreement, then a transfer by the route the group gives, fetched as a grid job on the owner's word.
